_about: Posture check: 8 band tests (classic v4.0) + 5 bodyweight tests (v4.6). Text and options only — grading is app/js/engine/posture.js (keyed by id). pattern: apt (pelvis & core / anterior pelvic tilt), hips (hip rotation & glute control), head (forward head), back (hunched upper back / thoracic kyphosis), shoulders (rounded shoulders). Never rename an id or an option value: they are stored in the user's history. Thresholds revised after the physio review (docs/reviews/PHYSIO-REVIEW-2026-11.md), check v3.
painOptions: My usual back ache went up during the test
Pain, pins and needles or numbness into the arm

tests.name: Tilt Control Test
tests.equipment: Long band anchored behind your head
tests.setup: On your back, knees bent, feet flat. Light long band anchored behind your head, one end in each hand, arms straight up. Exhale and gently tip the pelvis so the low back gets heavy on the floor — small range only, do not flatten forcefully. Hold the tilt while breathing normally.

inputs.label: What happened
options: Back stayed gently pressed, breathing normally
Could hold, but had to hold my breath
Back arched off the floor — could not keep the tilt
Shaking hard in the first seconds

planChange.Clear: No change — tilt work stays at maintenance in the morning block.
planChange.Mild: No dose change at Mild — retest in 4 weeks; the tilt drill joins the morning block daily at Moderate.
planChange.Moderate: Supine pelvic tilt drill joins the morning Tilt block daily, before the dead bug.
planChange.Priority: Daily tilt drill + dead bug regressed to toe-taps; band promotion for pull-through is held until retest; flag for your physio.

tests.name: Dead Bug Control Test
tests.setup: On your back, arms up holding the band anchored behind your head, hips and knees at 90°. Lower one leg slowly toward the floor and return. Count clean reps per side — use the worse side.

inputs.label: What happened
options: Low back stayed heavy on the floor
Low back arched off the floor

planChange.Mild: No dose change at Mild — retest in 4 weeks.
planChange.Moderate: The morning Tilt block regresses the dead bug (toe-tap regression note) until retest.
planChange.Priority: The morning Tilt block replaces the dead bug with toe-taps only until the retest.

tests.name: Hip Internal Rotation Test (banded)
tests.equipment: Loop band around the ankles · chair
tests.setup: Sit tall on a firm chair, knees at 90°, loop band around the ankles. Thigh pinned still, rotate the shin OUTWARD (the hip turns inward). Judge each side against its own heel: full ≈ the foot travels its whole arc. A phone level app against the shin reads the angle from vertical.

inputs.label: What happened
options: Trunk leaned away to fake it

planChange.Clear: IR work stays in the maintenance rotation.
planChange.Mild: No plan change at Mild — retest in 4 weeks; the daily IR block starts at Moderate.
planChange.Moderate: The daily Hip IR block joins the morning plan, deficit side first, and IR work enters the corrective pool.
planChange.Priority: Daily IR block, deficit side first; 90/90 work is switches only — the lift-off progression is gated off until retest; flag the capsule question for your physio.

tests.name: Pallof Hold Test
tests.equipment: Long band anchored at chest height
tests.setup: Stand side-on to the anchor, band at the sternum, feet hip-width. Press straight out and hold. Test both sides — grade by the worse one.

inputs.label: What happened
options: Trunk kept turning toward the anchor

planChange.Mild: No plan change at Mild — retest in 4 weeks.
planChange.Moderate: No slot change at Moderate — treat as a warning: one more step down and Pallof goes half-kneeling with an extra bird-dog set.
planChange.Priority: Pallof goes half-kneeling only, and the daily Big 3 block adds a second bird-dog set.

tests.name: Glute Med Wall Test
tests.equipment: Loop band above the knees · wall
tests.setup: Loop band above the knees. Stand side-on, about a forearm's length from the wall. Stand on the leg FURTHER from the wall — that is the side being tested. Lift the near-wall knee to hip height and press the outside of that knee into the wall. Pelvis level, trunk upright. Hold, then turn round for the other side. Grade by the worse side.

inputs.label: What happened
options: Trunk leaned over the standing leg
Pelvis dropped on the free side
Felt it in the front of the hip, not the buttock

planChange.Clear: Glute med work stays as programmed.
planChange.Mild: No plan change at Mild — retest in 4 weeks.
planChange.Moderate: The glute inhibition finding drives the plan: clamshell runs weaker-side-twice and glute med work enters the corrective pool.
planChange.Priority: Clamshell goes supported-only with the worse side doubled, a guarding finding is added, and single-leg work stays supported until retest.

tests.name: Pull-Apart Endurance Test
tests.setup: Stand tall, arms straight ahead at shoulder height holding the lightest long band. Pull apart to the chest and return slowly. Count clean reps — stop at form loss, not exhaustion.

inputs.label: What happened
options: Low back arched to finish reps

planChange.Mild: Pull-aparts stay in the daily activation block.
planChange.Moderate: The rounded-shoulders finding drives the corrective pool (pull-aparts, face pulls, rows).
planChange.Priority: Upper-back work is a plan priority, and band promotion for pull-apart and face pull is blocked until retest.

tests.name: Wall Slide Test (banded)
tests.setup: Back on the wall — head, upper back, tailbone touching — mini-band around the wrists, forearms on the wall. Slide up into a narrow V and back down. Count clean reps.

inputs.label: What happened
options: Low back kept leaving the wall
Head poked forward off the wall

planChange.Mild: Scapular wall slides join the morning Posture block, 1 × 10.
planChange.Moderate: Scapular wall slides join the morning Posture block daily.
planChange.Priority: Wall slides join the Posture block daily — no band until the retest.

tests.name: Chin Tuck Test (banded)
tests.equipment: Lightest long band behind the head
tests.setup: Sit tall, lightest long band behind the head held in both hands. Glide the head straight back into the band — a double-chin glide, NOT a nod down. Count clean reps.

inputs.label: What happened
options: Front of the neck took over / head jutted
Head tilted down instead of gliding

planChange.Clear: Chin tucks stay in the desk rotation.
planChange.Mild: Chin tucks stay daily in the Posture block.
planChange.Moderate: Deep neck flexor holds join the morning Posture block, and the forward-head finding drives the corrective pool.
planChange.Priority: Deep neck flexor holds join the Posture block daily; chin tucks stay unbanded in the test until retest.

tests.name: Occiput-to-Wall Test
tests.setup: Stand with heels, buttocks and upper back against a wall. Look straight ahead with your chin level — eyes on the horizon, do not tip your chin up. Do NOT arch your low back to get your shoulders or head onto the wall; a hand-flat gap at the low back is normal. Stop if your back complains. Feel (or have someone check) the gap between the back of your head and the wall.

inputs.label: Back of the head
options: Touches only if I tip my chin up, or a 1-finger gap

inputs.label: Upper back
options: Both shoulder blades rest on the wall

planChange.Mild: Wall posture resets join the desk routine.
planChange.Moderate: The hunched-upper-back block (open book, wall slides, rows) joins the daily plan.
planChange.Priority: The upper-back block is daily and starts at Reset: thoracic mobility before any loaded rows; retest in 2 weeks. A gap this size can be partly structural — show your physio; not all of it will change with exercise.

tests.evidence: Occiput-to-wall distance is a standard clinical screen for thoracic kyphosis and forward head carriage.

tests.name: Deep Neck Flexor Endurance
tests.setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, a folded towel under your head. Start a phone timer, tuck your chin gently (a small double chin), and lift your head just off the towel. The test ENDS when the tuck is lost, your chin pokes, or your head touches the towel for more than a second. Stop at 60 s.

inputs.label: What ended it (recorded, not graded)
options: Reached 60 s, or stopped by choice
Tuck lost / chin poked (the normal end)

planChange.Clear: Chin tucks stay in the desk rotation.
planChange.Moderate: Deep neck flexor holds join the daily plan and the forward-head block drives part of every session.
planChange.Priority: Deep neck flexor work starts at Reset (supported, short holds) every day; retest in 2 weeks.

tests.evidence: Deep neck flexor endurance test (Harris et al. 2005): healthy adults averaged about 39 s, people with neck pain about 24 s (see also Domenech et al. 2011). Graded on time only.

tests.name: Supine Shoulder Height (pec minor)
tests.setup: Lie on your back, arms by your sides, palms up, and let the shoulders sink. Stand a bank card on its long edge on the floor next to your shoulder (it is 5.4 cm tall). Have someone look, or film from floor level at your side: how high is the back of the bony tip of your shoulder above the floor?

inputs.label: RIGHT shoulder
options: Between 1 finger-width and the card’s height (2.5–5 cm)

inputs.label: LEFT shoulder
options: Between 1 finger-width and the card’s height (2.5–5 cm)

planChange.Clear: No chest-opening work needed beyond warm-ups.
planChange.Mild: Doorway chest stretch joins the daily posture block.
planChange.Moderate: Chest opening (doorway, standing opener) daily plus band pull-aparts and face pulls 3× a week.
planChange.Priority: Chest opening (doorway, standing opener) daily plus band pull-aparts and face pulls 3× a week.

tests.evidence: Acromion height in lying is a common screen for a short pec minor, but it is poor at telling short from normal (Lewis & Valentine 2007; about 2.5 cm is normal, Sahrmann 2002). It is used only as a minor sign and never grades Priority.

tests.name: Overhead Reach Test
tests.setup: Lie on your back, feet flat, knees bent, low back gently heavy on the floor (ribs down). Keep your arms straight, thumbs up, and raise them overhead toward the floor behind you — measure only as far as your ribs stay down. If it pinches your low back or shoulder, stop.

inputs.label: Where your hands land
options: Thumbs touch the floor, ribs stayed down
Short by less than a hand-width
Short by a hand-width or more
Couldn't keep my ribs down at all

planChange.Mild: Wall slides join the posture block.
planChange.Moderate: Open books and wall slides daily; overhead work stays ribs-down only.
planChange.Priority: Open books and wall slides daily; overhead work stays ribs-down only.

tests.evidence: Supine shoulder-flexion range with the lumbar spine controlled reflects thoracic extension and lat length — limited range is typical of a hunched upper back.

tests.name: Seated Thoracic Rotation
tests.setup: Sit tall on a chair, a pillow squeezed between your knees, feet flat, a broom handle across the front of your shoulders. Lay your phone flat on your breastbone with the compass open and note the starting reading. Turn slowly to each side; stop before your low back or hips join in. Never bounce.

planChange.Moderate: Open books daily, stiffer side first.
planChange.Priority: Thoracic rotation mobility twice daily, stiffer side first; the lumbar spine must not make up the difference.

tests.evidence: Seated rotation with the pelvis fixed is a reliable thoracic measure (Johnson et al. 2012). Unloaded and slow — never a loaded twist.
